title: Who Ran Up the Inference Bill? AI Traffic Control with KServe and Gateway API Inference Extensions
tldr: A beginner-level talk on attributing and controlling inference spend by putting an AI-aware gateway in front of KServe models. A live demo on kind uses agentgateway with the Gateway API Inference Extension to log tokens per team, enforce per-team token budgets, block sensitive data and fail over to a cloud LLM.

key_points.text: Inference bills show a total but not which team or service spent the tokens, and request counts mislead because token use per request varies widely.
Inference traffic differs from classic traffic: seconds to minutes, streamed token by token, costly, routed on the body, so request limits and round-robin balancing stop working.
KServe creates the HTTPRoute, InferencePool and endpoint picker from one model resource.
The endpoint picker chooses pods using KV cache, prefix and LoRA adapter state instead of load alone.
Any gateway that supports the Inference Extension works; the demo uses agentgateway as the AI-aware gateway.
Local models need a cost too; a rough GPU-hours-over-tokens figure is enough to visualize spend.
Plain Gateway API logs show only status codes; with the inference extension, logs include input and output tokens and the model.
Per-team traffic showed the team with the fewest requests spent the most tokens.
A guardrail rejected a prompt containing a credit card number at the gateway; a team past its token budget got 429s while other teams kept working.
When the local model returned 500, the gateway failed over to a cloud LLM without interrupting users.
Takeaways: meter tokens not requests, put a name on every token, control spend at the gateway, build on standards and keep policy thin.

numbers.text: Example per-team budget: 60,000 tokens, after which requests get HTTP 429.
Mock LLM log entry: 6 input tokens, 1 output token.
The ML research team sent only 3 requests but spent the most tokens.

open_gaps.text: Per-token cost for self-hosted models is a rough estimate, not a production calculation.
Classic request limits and round-robin load balancing do not fit token-based inference traffic.
Standard Gateway API logs carry no token or model data without an inference-aware gateway.

opportunities.text: Add per-team token budgets and failover to a cloud model at your AI gateway.
Run the speaker's kind-based demo repo with KServe and agentgateway.
Export gateway token logs to your monitoring stack to split the inference bill by team.
